newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Russia defence ministers urge friendship.
newsitem.headline: China, Russia defence ministers urge friendship.

text.p: Chinese and Russian defence ministers have hailed increasing trust and friendship in ties between the two neighbours who were once bitter socialist rivals, China's Xinhua news agency reported.

Current growth in Sino-Russian relations is "in the fundamental interests of the people of both countries", Xinhua quoted Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian as telling his visiting Russian counterpart Igor Rodionov on Monday.
Improving ties were "conducive to peace, stability, and development of the Asia-Pacific and the world as a whole", Chi was quoted as saying.
Rodionov's visit, just days before Chinese President Jiang Zemin is to go to Moscow, would help maintain and develop the friendship between their two armed forces, Chi said.

"We are ready to usher in the 21st century together with our Russian friends... to enable our two countries to become good neighbours, good partners, and good friends forever and to push forward the strategic cooperative partnership between our two countries," Chi said.

Rodionov was to discuss military cooperation, including an exchange of visits, but talks would not involve technical cooperation, an embassy spokesman said. The Russian defence minister arrived on Sunday for a five-day visit.
Talks also would not touch on arms sales and no documents would be signed during the trip, the embassy spokesman said.
Rodionov said the Sino-Russian friendship had set a good example for the rest of the world, lauding the greater stability derived from good ties between the two neighbours, Xinhua said.
"This mutually beneficial cooperation is not directed at a third nation," Rodionov was quoted as saying, apparently addressing some international fears of a new Sino-Russia axis.

The visit is the latest sign of warming relations between the two countries, coming just prior Jiang's planned visit to Moscow, scheduled for April 22-26. Jiang's trip is aimed at building closer ties after decades of distrust and would step up Russian efforts to strengthen relations in the East.
Next week Jiang is expected to sign initial agreements with his Russian counterpart Boris Yeltsin on reducing troop strengths along their common borders.
The summit, which will set the maximum number of troops to be deployed within 100 km (60 miles) of the border would also be attended by representatives of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan.
